Package com.egradx.notification.spi

Interface EgradxDeliveryResult

All Known Implementing Classes:
EgradxDeliveryResult.Permanent, EgradxDeliveryResult.Retryable, EgradxDeliveryResult.Sent
public sealed interface EgradxDeliveryResult permits EgradxDeliveryResult.Sent, EgradxDeliveryResult.Retryable, EgradxDeliveryResult.Permanent
What happened when a channel tried to deliver one message to one address.

The distinction between EgradxDeliveryResult.Retryable and EgradxDeliveryResult.Permanent is the whole point: "the SMTP server is down" and "that address does not exist" call for opposite responses, and a channel is the only thing that can tell them apart. A channel that cannot tell should answer retryable — the dispatcher gives up after the configured number of attempts either way, so a wrong "retryable" costs a few wasted attempts while a wrong "permanent" silently loses a message that would have gone out.

A channel that throws instead of returning is treated as retryable.
